analysis_notes.summary: Torah #107 is a brief homiletical argument against sexual desire. Rebbe Nachman contrasts eating (which adds vitality) with lust (which diminishes it), concluding that the sexual drive is needed only for procreation. The teaching is entirely eitza-structured (cause-and-effect reasoning and practical advice). There are no bechina statements — no concept is declared to be 'an aspect of' another. Therefore no packages can be formed from this torah.
